sql:
SELECT COUNT(1) AS n
FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

attempts.sql: SELECT COUNT(1) AS n FROM TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL
attempts.change_summary: Removed the unnecessary LEFT JOIN to promotion table since no promotion columns are referenced in SELECT and the join cannot affect the row count of a LEFT JOIN when only counting rows from the left table.

diagnosis.bottleneck: The left outer join to the tiny promotion table (300 rows) is unnecessary for the COUNT(*) result, yet the plan broadcasts promotion and performs a hash join for every qualifying store_sales row, adding CPU and memory overhead.

plan_nodes.note: LeftOuter BuildRight; Left keys [1]: [ss_promo_sk#48983]; Right keys [1]: [p_promo_sk#48998]; Join type: LeftOuter; Join

hypotheses.claim: A LEFT JOIN whose columns are never read still costs a join; if the joined key is unique it cannot change the rows and can be removed. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk)

The BroadcastHashJoin builds a hash table from the 300-row promotion table and probes it for each row from store_sales that passes the ss_customer_sk IS NULL filter; removing the join would eliminate this work without changing the result.

The Parquet scan pushes the IsNull(ss_customer_sk) filter, but if the column statistics do not effectively prune row groups (e.g., nulls are widespread), the scan may still read a large fraction of the store_sales table.

The Exchange (SinglePartition) collects partial counts from all partitions to a single node for final aggregation; this shuffle is small but could be avoided if the join were removed and the count pushed down further.
